I reviewed the memory store's `atlas` entries (120 live claims total, ~108 facts / 9 instructions / 3 lessons). Ran the automated consolidation scan, then manually cross-checked the raw claims since the scan only flags *textually similar* pairs — it can't catch contradictions worded differently. Nothing has been changed. Here's what I found:

## Real contradiction (the important one)
- **"Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically."** directly conflicts with **"Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs `bin/ship.sh --staging` by hand."**
  These can't both be true. The automated scan missed this pair entirely because the wording is too different for its similarity metric — I only caught it by reading the full deploy-related set manually.

## Likely duplicates (same fact, reworded)
- "Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used." ≈ "The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test." (0.98 similarity — near-identical)
- "Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root." ≈ "To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo." (0.95 similarity — near-identical)
- A third ship.sh claim — "Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone." — overlaps with the above two but adds a unique fact (the old `make deploy` target was removed), so it's a partial duplicate rather than a pure one.

## Suspicious / worth a closer look
- Three separate claims about "feature flags" that may describe two *different* things under one name:
  - "Feature flags in atlas are additive only, so `cargo check --all-features` has to pass" (sounds like Cargo compile-time features)
  - "Feature flags in atlas are an environment variable map and nothing more"
  - "A flag in atlas is deleted within a month of full rollout" (sounds like a runtime rollout flag)
  Either these are genuinely two systems both loosely called "feature flags" (confusing but not wrong), or one of them is stale/incorrect. Worth confirming before handoff.

## Stale (overdue for cleanup by their own rules)
- "The branch under review is spike/consolidate." — filed as short-lived (`fast` decay), hasn't been touched in 40 days, clearly outdated.
- "The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api." — same issue, "this week" long past.

## Noise, not real findings
The automated scan's `near_duplicates` list grouped 8 unrelated facts (license, status page, image tags, distroless base, unprivileged user, etc.) into one cluster at a low 0.84 minimum similarity. The tool's own caveat applies here: this is chaining through a middle claim, not 8 claims saying the same thing — I'd ignore that cluster. Same goes for most of the "contradictions" list beyond the two duplicate pairs and the one real contradiction above — pairs like "images pushed to GHCR" vs "container built from distroless base" are just topically adjacent, not conflicting or redundant.

Want me to fix any of these (merge the duplicates, resolve the staging-deploy contradiction, forget the two stale scaffolding notes)? I'd need your call on which staging-deploy claim is actually true.
